$comment: Registry of substrate the platform has RETIRED. Consumed by
Why this exists: when BET-5 retired Neo4j and Qdrant onto PostgreSQL, the
code changed and the published docs did not. /architecture/platform-overview/
kept describing Neo4j as a live service, and the disaster-recovery runbook kept
telling operators mid-incident to restore a database that no longer exists.
Nothing failed, because no gate was watching the words.
The doc-impact graph narrows this, but its edges are OPT-IN — it only protects
pages someone remembered to annotate. This registry is the complement: it needs
no annotation on the page at all. Add one entry here when you retire something,
and every live doc still naming it becomes net-new breakage on the next PR.
TO RETIRE SOMETHING: add an entry, run `pnpm check:retired-substrate`, and fix
or explicitly baseline every page it surfaces. Expect a long list the first
time — that list is the blast radius you would otherwise have shipped past.

retired.replacement: the Postgres graph mirror — graph_node / graph_edge, traversed in packages/db/src/pg-graph.ts
